subject: Discovery recap: open-model gap analysis & recommended next steps
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Sam Tu <sam.tu@keplerhealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-14T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery recap: open-model gap analysis & recommended next steps

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for a productive discovery today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

1) Primary goals you stated
- Extract structured clinical fields from visit notes (meds, dosages, diagnoses) with high precision for downstream analytics.
- Keep PII/PHI strictly controlled (prefer on-prem or VPC-only processing for production).
- Cost target: lower per-token inference cost than your current proprietary baseline without regression in accuracy.

2) Our recommended evaluation plan (short version)
- Models to trial: Llama2-13B (Q8), Falcon-40B-Instruct (Q4_0 if available), and Redwood-Prod-7B (our proprietary baseline for comparison).
- Benchmarks we’ll run: entity extraction F1 (primary), exact-match on key-value pairs (secondary), and latency p95 at 512-token context.
- Acceptance thresholds (initial proposal): entity F1 >= 0.90, structured EM >= 0.92, latency p95 < 250ms (for dedicated deployment).

3) Logistics / governance
- Proposed eval: 2-week sandbox run using a deidentified sample you provide; option to run on-prem if required for PHI.
- We’ll provide prompt set v1 (attached) + a starter prompt engineering guide.
- We’ll deliver a bench report and suggested roll-forward config (quantization, batching, cache policy).

4) Next steps (mutual action plan)
- You: confirm sample size and whether we should pursue on-prem vs VPC (cc: procurement).
- Us: spin up eval infra and share benchmark link + initial run within 5 business days.
- Schedule 30-min kickoff: propose Tue 9/16 or Wed 9/17.

Risks to call out: aggressive quantization (Q4/Q8) can introduce subtle hallucinations on low-frequency clinical tokens; we’ll include checks to flag regressions. If you want, we can run ensemble fallback to Redwood-Prod-7B for high-risk extraction fields during the trial.

Attachments: prompt_set_v1.csv, benchmark-run-20260914.pdf (sample report template).

Link to starter docs: https://drive.google.com/open?id=abc123benchmark
HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.com/deal/KEP-2026-042

If that all looks right, I’ll queue the infra work and loop in our compliance contact for the PHI handling checklist.

—Priyom
Priyom Das

Thanks Priyom — that matches my notes. A couple quick clarifications before we kick off: 

- PHI: For the initial eval we can provide a deidentified sample (10k notes). If early results look good, we’ll need an on-prem option for production.
- Fallbacks: the ensemble fallback sounds promising for safety-critical fields.
- Procurement: looping in procurement to flag potential contract terms (SLA, data residency).

We’re good to start the 2-week sandbox. Can you confirm the size of compute you’ll need so procurement can provision budget? Also, can you provide a TOC for what will be included in the benchmark-run PDF?

Sam Tu

sam.tu@keplerhealth.com

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Sam Tu <sam.tu@keplerhealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, procurement@keplerhealth.com
Date: 2026-09-15T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: open-model gap analysis & recommended next steps

Thanks Sam — answering inline: 

- Compute: For the 10k-note deidentified sample we recommend the following trial profile: 1 x A10G (or equivalent) for ingest + 2 x A100-80GB for parallel inference (ephemeral for 2 weeks). Estimated cost ballpark will be in the quote we send to procurement, but it’s modest for the short trial. If you need stricter cost controls, we can run a reduced config (1 x A100 + longer wall time).

- Benchmark TOC (what you’ll see in the PDF): executive summary, dataset description, metric definitions (F1/EM/latency), per-model confusion matrices, prompt sets used, failure-case examples, and recommended roll-forward config (quantization, batching, cache policy).

Model comparison notes (high-level):
- Llama2-13B (Q8): lowest cost-to-run; good on common clinical phrasing, may struggle with rare abbreviations.
- Falcon-40B-Instruct (Q4_0): best out-of-the-box instruction following for long contexts; higher memory footprint but stronger recall on free-text fields.
- Redwood-Prod-7B (proprietary baseline): slightly higher cost but typically more consistent on low-frequency tokens due to curated tokenization and post-processing heuristics.

Quality regression concerns: aggressive quantization and kernel-fusion optimizations can drop F1 by ~1–3 points on low-frequency entities. Our plan: run a side-by-side A/B on a stratified holdout and automatically flag any field where open model F1 < baseline F1 - 0.01, at which point we trigger fallback or tighten prompts.

Links: starter prompts + metrics: https://drive.google.com/open?id=abc123benchmark
Proposal doc: https://docsend.com/d/kepler-eval-proposal
HubSpot: https://hubspot.com/deal/KEP-2026-042

I’ll attach prompt_set_v1.csv and a blank benchmark-run template. Are you good with the kickoff on Wed 9/16 at 10am PT?

—Priyom

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-15T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Discovery recap: open-model gap analysis & recommended next steps

Fwd’ing Sam’s confirmation and the plan — quick asks for the infra/ops + research side: 

Neha / David — can you confirm the following items before I lock the kickoff: 
- Recommended quantization profile to trial first (Neha: Q8 vs Q4_0 tradeoffs) and expected accuracy delta we should expect.
- A/B harness: can we run a stratified 2k holdout with automatic rollback if F1 drop > 0.01 on any critical field?
- Instrumentation: please include per-field diffing + token-level attention to help us diagnose hallucinations.

Technical notes for the trial (paste for visibility):
```
prompt: "Extract medication, dosage, and frequency from NOTE -- return JSON with fields: medication_name, dose, unit, frequency"
batch_size: 32
max_new_tokens: 256
use_kv_cache: true
quantization: start with Q8 for Llama2-13B; try Q4_0 for Falcon-40B on a separate runner
monitoring: emit per-request confidence scores + compare to baseline post-processing
```
Attachments: eval-runbook.md (internal runbook we’ll follow).

Thanks — Priyom

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-15T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Discovery recap: open-model gap analysis & recommended next steps

Thanks — quick alignment from infra/ops: 

- Quantization: start with Q8 on Llama2-13B for throughput. For Falcon-40B run Q4_0 on a separate node to compare. Expect ~1.0–2.5 F1 delta on rare tokens with Q8; Q4_0 may push delta to ~0.8–1.8 depending on prompt.
- A/B harness: we can automate rollback. Suggested sample: 2k stratified holdout (500 notes per clinical area). Automatic rollback trigger: any critical-field F1 drop > 0.012.
- Telemetry: will enable per-field diffs, token-level attention dumps for flagged failures, and log-level indicators for hallucination (low confidence + entity mismatch).
- Runbook: follow eval-runbook.md (attached). We’ll also include a short checklist for procurement re: ephemeral GPUs and data access audit logs.

I’ll provision the runners once procurement confirms budget. Priyom — if Sam approves Wed 9/16 10am PT we can use that slot to finalize run-level parameters.

—David
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference
